decisions.reason: After remaining in the assortment into 2025, this core safety-shoe line likely meets at least minimum aspirations, so a large incumbent with slack would usually keep developing it rather than withdraw it quickly.
The comfort insole still supports the footwear system and cross-selling, but as a less central accessory it would be one of the first candidates for reallocation if its results stay below aspiration.

The supportive insole fits customer needs, yet its overlap with other insole offerings makes it comparatively more vulnerable to problemistic search and portfolio simplification if performance disappoints.
An ergonomic safety-shoe series with visible managerial emphasis remains close to the firm’s innovation path, so continued retention is very likely unless results clearly fall short of expectations.

Firefighter and rescue boots are a specialized but capability-consistent extension, so they are likely to be kept while niche demand is tested, though they remain less protected than the main safety-footwear lines.
Because the moulded insole was framed as a flagship direction, management would normally continue backing it and tolerate uncertainty unless evidence of underperformance became unmistakable.
